name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run a 5% A/B test for the new feature with users who opted in. This keeps risk low while giving us real data on performance and bugs before scaling. The trade-off is slower user exposure, but it prevents a bad rollout from hurting the 95% who aren’t in the test.

name: Gauge
text: Self-selection bias in the 5% cohort means you’re only learning how *willing* users react, not how *all* users would. A 10% blind rollout to opted-in users still skews toward early adopters—better to run a 10% *random* sample across the full user base to measure true impact. Settle it with a pre-commit analysis: compare user segment baselines (engagement, churn) between the 10% random group and the rest to confirm no hidden skew.
